title: Vimokkharam Accounts
kicker: Vimokkharam Forest Hermitage Inc · Olinda, Victoria
cpiName: the Australian consumer price index (World Bank, yearly average; for a year to 30 June, the average of the two calendar years it spans)
costDefShort: the total expenses the charity reports to the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) each year, which can include wear on buildings (depreciation).
defs: Spending: the total expenses Vimokkharam Forest Hermitage Inc reports to the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) in its yearly Annual Information Statement; the statement does not separate wear on buildings (depreciation) or the kinds of cost. Residents: the monks, novices, nuns and anagārikas listed at Vimokkharam on the community lists, on average; guests and lay residents are not counted. Inflation: the Australian consumer price index (World Bank). All amounts in Australian dollars, as paid at the time, unless the page says "in today's money".
holdLede: The statement also gives what the charity owns and owes at the end of each year.
holdSub: Net assets: everything the charity owns less everything it owes, at the end of each year.

incomeNote: Income moves a lot from year to year; the statement does not say why.

notes: Where the figures come from. Vimokkharam Forest Hermitage Inc (Australian business number 73 051 793 658) is a registered charity. Its yearly totals come from the ACNC's published Annual Information Statement data for the years 2017 to 2024 (acnc_ais.csv in this folder keeps the rows for this charity).
Years. The charity's year runs from 1 July to 30 June. It is named by the year it ends in: "2024" is July 2023 to June 2024.

What the statement shows. Total income, total expenses, total assets and total liabilities. It has no cost lines and does not separate wear on buildings (depreciation), so nothing is taken out of spending and this page cannot show what the money went on.
Money in. Total gross income as reported. Some of it can be given for a set purpose, such as building work, which the statement does not show.

The 2021 assets figure. The 2021 statement gives total assets of $74,249,984 and net assets of $74,236,660. Assets are about $0.6 to $1.8 million in the other years, so this looks like a data-entry error and the two figures are left out. The charity's income and spending for 2021 are used as reported.
Not in the accounts. Food, and much of the work done for a monastery, is given by supporters and is not a cost line.
Residents are the monks, novices, nuns and anagārikas on the community lists. Guests, retreatants and lay residents are not counted.
